title: Azure Reservations and Savings Plans - Simply Explained

entities.name: Microsoft Azure
entities.quote: Azure advertises up to seventy two percent off your cloud bill, but that number hides a catch.

entities.name: Microsoft
entities.quote: Reservations and savings plans are how Microsoft sells that price cut

entities.name: Azure Cosmos DB
entities.quote: for Azure files, and for cosmos DB throughput

entities.name: Azure Files
entities.quote: There are reservations for virtual machines, for blob storage capacity, for Azure files

quotes.text: A smaller discount that matches your usage beats a bigger discount that doesn't. Every single time. Stretching for the deepest rate is how people end up paying for capacity they never touch.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Condenses the episode's core lesson that utilization matters more than the headline discount.

quotes.text: A discount is a rate, and a rate only saves you money on usage that exists. No usage means no saving, no matter how deep the percentage looks on the page.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable reframing of commitment discounts for cost decisions.

quotes.text: If you promised five dollars for this hour and only use three, the other two are gone and you don't get them back next hour or next month.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the use-it-or-lose-it mechanic of savings plans concrete.

quotes.text: Scope also explains why people end up with an unused discount. It decides where the benefit is allowed to land and not what you're allowed to run.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies a common misunderstanding about reservation scope.

quotes.text: A good rule for a beginner is to earn your way up. Start with the shorter term. Watch how your usage actually behaves for a year and let that evidence decide whether the longer commitment deserves your money.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear, actionable recommendation on choosing commitment terms.

chapters.title: Why pay before you use it
Which one fits and how long to commit

takeaways: Reservations give the deepest discount for stable workloads tied to one resource type, size and region, while savings plans trade a smaller discount for flexibility across services and regions.
Whether a commitment pays off depends on how much of it you actually use, not on the advertised discount percentage.
Start with shorter terms and shared scope, use Azure's usage-based recommendations as evidence, and remember that licensing, networking and storage are not discounted.
hook: Azure promises up to seventy-two percent off, but commitment discounts can quietly turn into money you already spent. This episode explains Azure Reservations and savings plans in plain words for anyone who pays or plans an Azure bill. You will learn which option fits your workload, how term and scope affect risk, and the one number that decides whether a commitment is worth it.
